pp:ce:2024:q5-s2.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 2 | Question: 5
pp:ce:2024:q5-s2.question:
Consider two ordinary differential equations (ODEs):

$P: \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{x^{4}+3 x^{2} y^{2}+2 y^{4}}{x^{3} y}$
$\mathrm{Q}: \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\frac{-\mathrm{y}^{2}}{\mathrm{x}^{2}}$

Which one of the following options is CORRECT?
options: P is a homogeneous ODE and Q is an exact ODE.
P is a homogeneous ODE and Q is not an exact ODE.
P is a nonhomogeneous ODE and Q is an exact ODE.
P is a nonhomogeneous ODE and Q is not an exact ODE.

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Ordinary Differential Equation
detailed_solution.markdown:
$P: \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{x^{4}+3 x^{2} y^{2}+2 y^{4}}{x^{3} y}$

$\frac{d y}{d x}=\left(\frac{x^{4}}{x^{3} y}\right)+\left(\frac{3 x^{2} y^{2}}{x^{3} y}\right)+\left(\frac{2 y^{4}}{x^{3} y}\right)$

$\frac{d y}{d x}=\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)+3\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)+2\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^{3}$

$\frac{d y}{d x}=\left(\frac{1}{y / x}\right)+3\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)+2\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^{3}$

$\frac{d y}{d x}=f\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)$

So $P$ is a homogenous ODE

$\mathrm{Q}: \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\frac{-\mathrm{y}^{2}}{\mathrm{x}^{2}}$

$x^{2} d y=-y^{2} d x$

$y^{2} d x+x^{2} d y=0$

$M=y^{2} \quad \frac{d M}{\partial y}=2 y$

$N=x^{2} \quad \frac{\partial N}{\partial \mathrm{x}}=2 \mathrm{x}$

So $\mathrm{Q}$ is non exact $\mathrm{ODE}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ce:2024:q14-s2.question:
The following figure shows a plot between shear stress and velocity gradient for materials/fluids P, Q, R, S, and T.

Which one of the following options is CORRECT?
options: P $\rightarrow$ Ideal Fluid; Q $\rightarrow$ Ideal Bingham plastic; R $\rightarrow$ Non-Newtonian fluid; S $\rightarrow$ Newtonian fluid
P $\rightarrow$ Real solid; Q $\rightarrow$ Ideal Bingham plastic; S $\rightarrow$ Newtonian fluid; T $\rightarrow$ Ideal Fluid
P $\rightarrow$ Ideal Fluid; Q $\rightarrow$ Ideal Bingham plastic; R $\rightarrow$ Non-Newtonian fluid; T $\rightarrow$ Real solid
P $\rightarrow$ Real solid; Q $\rightarrow$ Newtonian fluid; R $\rightarrow$ Ideal Bingham plastic; T $\rightarrow$ Ideal Fluid

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Fluid Properties and Manometry
detailed_solution.markdown: Various types of newtonian \& non-newtonian fluids are shown in the figure. Fluids which obeys Newton's law of viscosity $\left(\tau=\mu \frac{\mathrm{du}}{\mathrm{dy}}\right)$ are called Newtonian Fluids and those fluids which do not obey this rule are called Non-Newtonian Fluids. General relationship between shear stress and velocity gradient is given by $\tau=\mathrm{A}\left(\frac{\mathrm{du}}{\mathrm{dy}}\right)^{\mathrm{n}}+\mathrm{B}$ In the figures shown above, slope of the curve is called apparent viscosity. Fluid for which apparent viscosity increases with du/dy are called Dilatant. Dilatant fluids are also called shear thickening fluids. Examples of dilatant fluids are solution with suspended starch or sand, sugar in water. Fluids for which apparent viscosity decreases with du/dy are called Pseudo Plastic. Pseudo plastic fluid are also called shear thinning fluid. Examples are paints, polymer solutions, blood, paper pulp, syrup, molasses, milk, gelatine. Bingham Plastic (ideal plastic) fluids require a certain minimum shear stress $t_{y}$ (yield stress) before they start flowing. Examples: tooth paste, sewage sludge, drilling mud have time dependent Newtonian Behaviour. Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

Three vectors $\vec{p}, \vec{q}$ and $\vec{r}$ are given as

$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$
$\vec{r}=2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}$

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Calculus
detailed_solution.markdown:
(A) $\vec{p} \times(\vec{q} \times \vec{r})=(\vec{p} \cdot \vec{r}) \vec{q}-(\vec{p} \cdot \vec{q}) \vec{r}$

(This is always true for any three given vectors)

(B) We know that $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}$ is always true but $\vec{a} \times \vec{b} \neq \vec{b} \times \vec{a}$ because $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=-\vec{b} \times \vec{a}$

This can be true only when $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=0$

So, $\quad \vec{r} \cdot(\vec{p} \times \vec{q})=\vec{r} .(\vec{q} \times \vec{p})$

$\vec{r} \cdot(\vec{p} \times \vec{q})=-\vec{r} \cdot(\vec{p} \times \vec{q})$

This can be true if

$$\begin{aligned}

\vec{r} \cdot(\vec{p} \times q) & =0 \\

\vec{p} \times \vec{q} & =\hat{i}-2 \hat{j}+j

\end{aligned}$$

$(\vec{r} \cdot \vec{p} \times \vec{q})=0$ this is true in this case

(C) $\vec{p} \times(\vec{q} \times \vec{r})$ can't be equal to $(\vec{p} \times \vec{q}) \times \vec{r}$ because

$\vec{p} \times(\vec{q} \times \vec{r}) \perp \vec{p}$ and $(\vec{p} \times \vec{q}) \times \vec{r}) \perp \vec{r}$

So, $(\vec{p} \times(\vec{q} \times \vec{r}) \neq(\vec{p} \times \vec{q})) \times \vec{r}$

(D) $\vec{p} \times(\vec{q} \times \vec{r})+\vec{q} \times(\vec{r} \times \vec{p})+\vec{r} \times(\vec{p} \times \vec{q})=\overrightarrow{0}$

$(\vec{p} . \vec{r}) \vec{q}-(\vec{p} . \vec{q}) \vec{r}+(\vec{q} . \vec{p}) \vec{p}-(\vec{q} \cdot \vec{r}) \vec{p}+(\vec{r} . \vec{q}) \vec{p}-(\vec{r} . \vec{q})) \vec{q}$

$0=0$

$$\begin{aligned}

& \vec{p} \cdot \vec{r}=\vec{r} \cdot \vec{p} \\

& \vec{p} \cdot \vec{q}=\vec{q} \cdot \vec{p} \\

& \vec{q} \cdot \vec{r}=\vec{r} \cdot \vec{q}

\end{aligned}$$

(Hence proved)

Therefore, the correct option(s) are **A, B, D**.

pp:ce:2024:q43-s2.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 2 | Question: 43
pp:ce:2024:q43-s2.question: A homogeneous earth dam has a maximum water head difference of $15 \mathrm{~m}$ between the upstream and downstream sides. A flownet was drawn with the number of potential drops as 10 and the average length of the element as $3 \mathrm{~m}$. Specific gravity of the soil is 2.65 . For a factor of safety of 2.0 against piping failure, void ratio of the soil is ____(rounded off to 2 decimal places).

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Properties of Soils
detailed_solution.markdown:
$(\Delta \mathrm{H})$ total head loss $=15 \mathrm{~m}$

$\left(n_{d}\right)$ number of equipotential drops $=10$

(I) length of flow field $=3 \mathrm{~m}$

(G) specific gravity $=2.65$

(FOS) factor of safety $=2$

(e) void ratio $=$ ?

$(\Delta h)$ equipotential drop of head

$$\begin{aligned}

& =\frac{\text { Total head loss }}{\text { no. of equipotential drop }} \\

\Delta \mathrm{h} & =\frac{\Delta \mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{d}}}=\frac{15}{10}=1.5 \mathrm{~m}

\end{aligned}$$

FOS against quick sand condition $=\frac{i_{c r}}{i}$

(i) hydraulic gradient $=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{l}}=\frac{1.5}{3}=0.5$

$2=\frac{i_{c r}}{0.5},\left(i_{c r}\right)$ ciritical hydraulic gradient $=1$

Critical hydraulic gradient $\left(\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{cr}}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{G}-1}{1+\mathrm{e}}=1=\frac{2.65-1}{1+\mathrm{e}}$

(e)void ratio $=0.65$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.65** (acceptable range: [0.63, 0.67]).

pp:ce:2024:q44-s2.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 2 | Question: 44
pp:ce:2024:q44-s2.question:

The relative density index of the in-situ sand is ______ (rounded off to 2 decimal places)

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Shallow Foundation and Bearing Capacity
detailed_solution.markdown:
maximum density $\left(\gamma_{\mathrm{d}}\right)_{\max }=1.8 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$

minimum density $\left(\gamma_{\mathrm{d}}\right)_{\min }=1.3 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$

specific gravity $(G)=2.7$

$\left(I_{D}\right)$ relative density $=\frac{\gamma_{d \max }\left(\gamma_{d}-\gamma_{d \min }\right)}{\gamma_{d}\left(\gamma_{d \max }-\gamma_{d \min }\right)}$

$\therefore \quad(n)$ percentage of voids

$=\frac{\left(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{v}}\right) \text { volume of voids } \times 100}{\left(\mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{T}}\right) \text { Total volume }}=50 \%$

Porosity( $n$ ) $=0.5$

void ratio (e) $=\frac{\mathrm{n}}{1-\mathrm{n}}=\frac{0.5}{1-0.5}=1$

$\left(\gamma_{\mathrm{d}}\right)_{\text {insitu }}=\frac{\mathrm{G} \cdot \gamma_{\mathrm{w}}}{1+\mathrm{e}}=\frac{2.7 \times 1}{1+1}=1.35 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$

$\left(I_{D}\right)=\frac{1.8(1.35-1.3)}{1.35(1.8-1.3)}=0.13$

Relative density $\left(I_{D}\right)=0.13$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.13** (acceptable range: [0.12, 0.14]).

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Shear Strength of Soil
detailed_solution.markdown: In stress-path triaxial testing, we can control both radial and axial stress. $$\begin{aligned} & \sigma_1=\sigma_3 \tan ^2\left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right)+2 \mathrm{C} \tan \left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right) \\ & 300=100 \tan ^2\left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right)+0\end{aligned}$$ [Since for drained test $C=0$ ] $\Rightarrow \phi=30^{\circ}$ Angle between normal to major plane and failure plane is $45+\frac{\phi}{2}$ Angle between normal to minor plane and failure plane is $45^{\circ}-\frac{\phi}{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ Angle between minor plane and failure plane $=45-\frac{\phi}{2}=45^{\circ}-\frac{30^{\circ}}{2}=30^{\circ}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **30**.

pp:ce:2024:q49-s2.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 2 | Question: 49
pp:ce:2024:q49-s2.question: A rectangular channel is $4.0 \mathrm{~m}$ wide and carries a discharge of $2.0 \mathrm{~m}^{3} / \mathrm{s}$ with a depth of $0.4 \mathrm{~m}$. detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
detailed_solution.markdown: width of channel $(B)=4 \mathrm{~m}$ discharge $(Q)=2 \mathrm{~m}^{3} / \mathrm{s}$ depth of $\operatorname{flow}(\mathrm{y})=0.4 \mathrm{~m}$ Specific energy at section (1) - (1) (E) $$\begin{aligned} & =\mathrm{y}_{1}+\frac{\mathrm{V}_{1}^{2}}{2 \mathrm{~g}} \\ & =0.4+\frac{\mathrm{Q}^{2}}{\mathrm{~B}_{1}^{2} \times 2 \mathrm{~g} \times \mathrm{y}_{1}^{2}} \\ & =0.4+\frac{2^{2}}{4^{2} \times 2 \times 9.81 \times 0.4^{2}} \\ & =0.4796 \mathrm{~m} \end{aligned}$$ When channel section is contracted to minimum width and for constant discharge Q. The flow over contracted section will be critical flow. $$\begin{aligned} E & =E_{c}=\frac{3}{2} \cdot y_{c} \\ \therefore \quad 0.4796 & =\frac{3}{2} \times y_{c} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \quad \quad y_{c} & =0.4796 \times \frac{2}{3}=0.3197 \mathrm{~m} \end{aligned}$$ For critical flow condition, $\frac{\mathrm{Q}^{2} \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{gA}^{3}}=1$ $\frac{\mathrm{Q}^{2} \mathrm{~B}_{\min }}{\mathrm{gB}_{\min \mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{c}}^{3}}^{3}}=1$ $$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{B}_{\min }^{2} & =\frac{\mathrm{Q}^{2}}{9 \mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{c}}^{3}}=1 \\ \mathrm{~B}_{\min } & =\left(\frac{\mathrm{Q}^{2}}{\mathrm{gy_{c } ^ { 3 }}}\right)^{1 / 3} \\ & =\left(\frac{2^{2}}{9.81 \times 0.3197^{3}}\right)^{1 / 2} \\ & =3.5325 \mathrm{~m} \simeq 3.53 \mathrm{~m} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **3.5** (acceptable range: [3.3, 3.7]).

pp:ce:2024:q50-s2.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 2 | Question: 50
pp:ce:2024:q50-s2.question: A circular settling tank is to be designed for primary treatment of sewage of a flow rate of 10 million liters/day. Assume a detention period of 2.0 hours and surface loading rate of 40000 liters $/ \mathrm{m}^{2} /$ day. The height (in meters) of the water column in the tank is _____ (rounded off to 2 decimal places)

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Treatment of Waste Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given,

Discharge, $\mathrm{Q}=10 \mathrm{MLD}$

Detention period, $\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{d}}=2 \mathrm{hr}$

Over flow rate, $\mathrm{V}_{0}=40,000$ litres $/ \mathrm{m}^{2} /$ day

$\mathrm{H}=$ ?

As, Surface area of tank $=\frac{\text { Discharge }}{\text { Over flow rate }}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{\mathrm{V}_{0}}$

So,

$$\begin{aligned}

& \text { S.A. }=\frac{10 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{~L} / \text { day }}{40,000 \mathrm{~L} / \mathrm{m}^{2} / \text { day }} \\

& \text { S.A }=250 \mathrm{~m}^{2}

\end{aligned}$$

Volume of tank $(V)=Q \times t_{d}$

$$\begin{aligned}

& =\frac{10 \times 10^{6} \times 10^{-3}}{24} \times 2 \mathrm{~m}^{3} \\

& \mathrm{~V}=833.33 \mathrm{~m}^{3}

\end{aligned}$$

Hence,

Height of water in tank or  Height of setting zone

$$\begin{aligned}

H & =\frac{833.33 \mathrm{~m}^{3}}{250 \mathrm{~m}^{2}} \\

H & =3.33 \mathrm{~m}

\end{aligned}$$

Note: In reality, height of water in tank OR height of settling zone is estimated by above approach but if the bottom of sedimentation tank is assumed to be sloping or hoppered (i.e sludge zone is also considered) then height of water in tank is determined as follows:

Using,

Volume of tank $(V)=D^{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{4} H+0.011 D\right)$

As,

$$\begin{aligned}

\text { S.A. } & =\frac{\pi}{4} D^{2}=250 \mathrm{~m}^{2} \\

D & =17.835 \mathrm{~m}

\end{aligned}$$

So, $833.33=(17.835)^{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{4} H+0.011(17.835)\right)$

So, $\mathrm{H}=3.085 \mathrm{~m}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **3.2** (acceptable range: [3, 3.4]).

pp:ce:2024:q52-s2.question:

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Railway and Airport Engineering
detailed_solution.markdown:
Constructed equillibrium cant

$=\frac{\mathrm{GV}_{\mathrm{eq}}^{2}}{127 \mathrm{R}}=\frac{1.75 \times 70^{2}}{127 \times 1080}=0.062518 \mathrm{~m}=62.52 \mathrm{~mm}$

With allowable cant deficiency of $100 \mathrm{~mm}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **114** (acceptable range: [112, 116]).

pp:ce:2024:q53-s2.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 2 | Question: 53
pp:ce:2024:q53-s2.question:
A vertical summit curve on a freight corridor is formed at the intersection of two gradients, $+3.0 \%$ and $-5.0 \%$.

Assume the following:
Only large-sized trucks are allowed on this corridor.
Design speed $=80 \mathrm{kmph}$
Eye height of truck drivers above the road surface $=2.30 \mathrm{~m}$
Height of object above the road surface for which trucks need to stop $=0.35 \mathrm{~m}$
Total reaction time of the truck drivers $=2.0 \mathrm{~s}$
Coefficient of longitudinal friction of the road $=0.36$
Stopping sight distance gets compesnated on the gradient.

The design length of the summit curve (in meters) to accommodate the stopping sight distance is _____ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).

primary.subtopicLabel: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
detailed_solution.markdown: Step 1: Algebraic difference of gradients $A = |+3 - (-5)| = 8% = 0.08$ Step 2: Conversion of speed $V = \frac{80 \times 1000}{3600} = 22.22 , \text{m/s}$ Step 3: Reaction distance $S_r = V \times t = 22.22 \times 2 = 44.44 , \text{m}$ Step 4: Braking distance $S_b = \frac{V^2}{2 g f} = \frac{(22.22)^2}{2 \times 9.81 \times 0.36} = 69.94 , \text{m}$ Step 5: Stopping Sight Distance (SSD) $S = S_r + S_b = 44.44 + 69.94 = 114.38 , \text{m}$ Step 6: Length of summit curve (SSD criterion) For summit curve, when $L \ge S$ $L = \frac{A S^2}{2(\sqrt{h_1} + \sqrt{h_2})^2}$ $\sqrt{h_1} = \sqrt{2.30} = 1.517, \quad \sqrt{h_2} = \sqrt{0.35} = 0.592$ $(\sqrt{h_1} + \sqrt{h_2})^2 = (2.109)^2 = 4.448$ $L = \frac{0.08 \times (114.38)^2}{2 \times 4.448} = \frac{1046.6}{8.896} = 117.70 , \text{m}$ Check condition: $L = 117.70 , \text{m} \ge S = 114.38 , \text{m}$ Hence, the condition is satisfied. Therefore, the correct answer is **118.5** (acceptable range: [117, 120]).

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

If the number of girls in classes VIII and IX is the same, then the number of girls in each class is

detailed_solution.concept: General Aptitude - Numerical Ability
detailed_solution.markdown:
Let no. of girls in $8^{\text {th }}=$ no. of girls in $9^{\text {th }}$

$=x$

$\frac{\text { No. of girls in } 8^{\text {th }} \text { class }}{\text { No. of girls in } 9^{\text {th }} \text { class }}=\frac{\text { No. of boys in } 9^{\text {th }} \text { class }}{\text { No. of girls in } 9^{\text {th }} \text { class }}$

$$\begin{aligned}

\frac{x}{450-x} & =\frac{360-x}{x} \\

x^{2} & =(450-x)(360-x) \\

x^{2} & =16200-450 x-360 x+x^{2} \\

x & =\left(\frac{16200}{810}\right) \\

& =200

\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.
